summary: Richard Sylvan was a philosopher who studied at Victoria University of Wellington (~1953–1958) and Princeton University (~1959–1963). He held posts at the University of Sydney (~1963–1964) and the Australian National University, where he became a fellow in 1971.

Richard Taupier works in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned an MS and a doctorate from the University of Massachusetts Amherst, where he served as Associate Director of Research Development, and was a visiting lecturer at Smith College.

Indologist Richard W. Lariviere studied at the University of Iowa and completed his Sanskrit doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher. His career includes serving as dean at UT Austin, provost at the University of Kansas, and president of both the University of Oregon and the Field Museum.

Sinologist Richard Wilhelm was educated at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium and the University of Tübingen (~1891–1895). He served as a guest professor at Peking University in 1923 and held the chair of Sinology at Goethe University Frankfurt starting in 1924, founding the institution in 1925.

Richard von Garbe worked in Indology and philosophy, studying under Hermann Günther Grassmann, Rudolf von Roth, and traditional teacher Bhagavata Acharya. After completing degrees at Tübingen and Königsberg, he served as Extraordinarius at Königsberg (1878–1894) and held a chair at Tübingen (1895–1927).

Richard von Glahn is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He became a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles around 1987 and served as a visiting fellow at the University of Tokyo from 1988 to 1989.
Rigdzin Shikpo was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under teachers Chögyam Trungpa and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.

Tibetologist Riika J. Virtanen pursued doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki under supervisors Asko Parpola, Klaus Karttunen, and Hannu K. Riikonen, and also studied under teacher Sangye Tandar Naga.

Rikizan Ishikawa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa University from around 1962 to 1973 and later served there as Professor of Buddhist Studies from circa 1975 to 1997.

Ringu Tulku is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who founded Bodhicharya. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, learning under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse, the 16th Karmapa, and Tubten Tsondru.
Rinzin Thargyal was a Tibetology scholar who completed his Magister degree at the University of Oslo in 1985, studying under Fredrik Barth and temporary supervisor Arne Martin Klausen.

Rita Langer, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, studied at SOAS, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and the University of Hamburg (PhD 2004) under Lambert Schmithausen and other mentors. She was affiliated with the University of Bristol in 2009.

Rita M. Gross, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, earned degrees from the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee and the University of Chicago. She spent most of her career at the University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire (~1973–1998) and served as head of Women and Religion at the AAR.

Rizong Sras Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who undertook monastic training at Drepung Loseling Monastery (1950–1959), studying under Tenzin Gyatso and others. He served as abbot of Samstanling Monastery, Gyume Tantric Monastery (~1979–1984), and Drepung Loseling (1984).

Rob Linrothe specializes in Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After earning his PhD from the University of Chicago in 1992, he held posts at the National Palace Museum, Skidmore College (1992–2009), the Rubin Museum of Art, and Northwestern University (2010–2022).

Rob Nairn was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied law and criminology at the University of Zimbabwe, King's College London, the University of Edinburgh, and the University of London. He held posts as senior lecturer at the University of Zimbabwe and professor at the University of Cape Town.

Robert A. F. Thurman studied at Harvard University (BA, MA, doctorate) and under Ngawang Wangyal and Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale. A specialist in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he founded the American Institute of Buddhist Studies and held professorships at Amherst College and Columbia University.
Robert Alan Goodding is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his PhD in 2002 from the University of Texas at Austin, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Patrick Olivelle.

Robert Alexander Neil was an Indology and linguistics scholar educated at the University of Aberdeen and Peterhouse, studying under mentors including William Duguid Geddes and Edward Byles Cowell. He was appointed University Lecturer in Sanskrit at Cambridge in 1884 and Fellow of Pembroke College in 1900.

Robert Anthony Orsi is a religious studies and history scholar who studied at Trinity College and Yale University. He held posts at Fordham, Indiana University, Harvard (2001–2007), Northwestern University (~2007), and the University of Notre Dame (2020–2021).
